newsitem.title: UK: Three NWE cat crackers go down, gasoline goes up.
newsitem.headline: Three NWE cat crackers go down, gasoline goes up.

text.p: Three catalytic crackers at three separate Northwest European refineries were shut down at the end of this week, crimping supplies in an already tight market.

Shell experienced problems at its Pernis refinery in Rotterdam, BP and Texaco encountered difficulties with their 55,000 barrel per day cat cracker at the Rotterdam Nerefco site and BP and Mobil's 60,000 bpd Coryton, U.K. cat cracker also went out of commission.

One of two catalytic crackers at Shell's Pernis refinery in Rotterdam went down for an unscheduled stoppage on Thursday for one month and a planned two month shut-down initially scheduled for the autumn will follow.
For August, September and October the unit will be out of action with the attendant loss of 100,000 tonnes of gasoline a month.
At the BP/Texaco Nerefco joint venture in Rotterdam the 55,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker was shut on Friday "for a few days" because of production problems, an official said.

BP and Mobil's 60,000 bpd Coryton, U.K. cat cracker has been shut-down for "essential maintenance following technical problems," according to a BP spokesman and will not be operational before the middle to end of next week.
The difficulties at the three refineries will exacerbate the current shortage of gasoline in Europe which combined with strong demand from the United States has seen prices propelled ever higher.
Delivered unleaded premium grade gasoline in NWE has risen $25 in the last two weeks from $190 a tonne to a touch over $215 on Friday.

Talk earlier this week that gasoline's European rally would start to ease with the approach of fresh cargoes from August 15-20 onwards has now quietened. Many dealers feel gasoline has room to head higher with a thirsty U.S. market scrabbling around for material that just is not available.
The Mediterranean market offers little succour since Italian, French and Romanian demand is thought to easily outstrip local supplies in August.
